title: Phone roll and flip into a desktop card
summary: A tall phone screen rolls a quarter turn with its tiled backdrop, flips over like a card and lands as a wide desktop screen while the camera pushes in. One continuous move says the product works on both.
use_when: Announcing that a mobile product now has a desktop or web version
A 5 s cross-platform beat inside a longer launch film
You have one mobile and one desktop screenshot and no motion footage
A light, calm, silent loop for a landing page or feed

look.type_style: rounded geometric sans, medium weight, size label 7 % H centred on each screen, tiny 3-line caption 1.5 % H below it

sfx.event: phone and backdrop roll a quarter turn
card flips from phone face to desktop face
desktop card settles after the push-in

structure.shot: blue portrait phone screen with a size label centred on pale blue, flanked by columns of light blue placeholder tiles
structure.camera: pull-out with roll: whole scene scales 1.00 -> 0.75 and rolls about -90 deg over 45 fr
structure.motion: phone and tile backdrop rotate together, -15 deg by f8, -60 deg by f23, -88 deg by f45; easings.inOutSine 45 fr (±0.25 s)

structure.shot: the landscape phone flips on its horizontal axis; its back face is a white desktop screen with a size label and caption
structure.camera: push-in starts: scale 1.00 -> 1.20 over 30 fr; residual roll -2 deg -> 0
structure.motion: flip 180 deg rotateX top edge first, blue face gone by f68, card aspect grows from 2.2:1 to 1.6:1 while flipping; tiles straighten into a level grid; springs.ui 30 fr (overshoot not measurable)

structure.shot: white wide desktop card centred, light blue tile rows above and below drifting off frame
structure.camera: push-in: card width 64 % -> 82 % of frame (scale 1.00 -> 1.28) over 45 fr, decelerating
structure.motion: camera only, springs.cameraIn 45 fr (overshoot not measurable); tiles leave top and bottom edges by f120

structure.shot: desktop card fills 82 % of the frame width on the pale blue ground, nothing else moves

params.brand: any brand.json: bg for the ground, accent for the phone face, surface for the desktop face and tiles
params.content.mobileScreen: portrait mobile screenshot (375x812 ratio) shown on the phone face
params.content.desktopScreen: 16:10 desktop screenshot shown on the back face
params.timing.flip: frames of the flip and aspect morph (default 30)
params.timing.push: frames of the push-in after the flip (default 45)

notes: Single continuous shot, 0 cuts, silent. Measured from 4 fps sheets (±0.25 s): roll ends ~f45, flip f45-f75, push-in f60-f120 (card width 53 % at 2.00 s, 64 % at 2.50 s, 73 % at 3.00 s, 79 % at 3.50 s, 82 % at 4.00 s), hold f120-f150. The tile backdrop rolls with the phone so the turn reads as a camera roll, not a spinning object. sfx planned by the glue rule, not measured. Proposed terms (not in vocabulary): camera-roll, card-flip, tile-backdrop.
